title: Phrasal verbs for Speaking
description: 40 phrasal verbs naturales que suben la nota de Lexical Resource en IELTS Speaking y TOEFL Interview.

cards.definition: 1) To raise a child. 2) To mention a topic.
cards.example: I was brought up in a small coastal town, so I've always loved the sea.

cards.definition: To spend your childhood somewhere; to become an adult.
cards.example: I grew up in Valencia, but I moved to Madrid for university.

cards.definition: To start a new hobby or activity.
cards.example: I took up running a couple of years ago to deal with stress.

cards.definition: To stop doing something.
cards.example: I had to give up playing the piano when I started working full-time.

cards.definition: To become interested in something.
cards.example: I got into photography when my uncle gave me his old camera.

cards.definition: To stay informed or at the same level/pace.
cards.es: mantenerse al día con; seguir el ritmo
cards.example: I try to keep up with the news by listening to podcasts on the bus.

cards.definition: To meet someone after a long time; to do work you missed.
cards.example: At weekends I usually catch up with old friends over coffee.

cards.definition: To feel happy about something that will happen.
cards.example: I'm really looking forward to travelling once my exams are over.
cards.warning: Va con -ing: 'look forward to seeing', NO 'to see'.

cards.definition: To find or meet by chance.
cards.example: I came across this little bookshop while I was wandering around the old town.

cards.definition: To finally be in a situation, often unplanned.
cards.example: We planned to go hiking, but we ended up staying in a café all afternoon.

cards.definition: To happen or be discovered in a particular way.
cards.example: The trip turned out to be one of the best experiences of my life.

cards.definition: To start a business or organisation.
cards.example: My cousin set up her own design company when she was only 25.

cards.definition: To do or complete a task.
cards.example: For my final project, I carried out a survey of 200 students.

cards.definition: To understand or solve.
cards.example: It took me a while to figure out how the metro system worked.

cards.definition: 1) To exercise. 2) To find a solution. 3) To end well.
cards.example: I work out at the gym three times a week; it was hard at first, but things have worked out well.

cards.definition: To have a good relationship.
cards.example: I get along really well with my younger brother, even though we're very different.

cards.definition: To admire and respect.
cards.example: I've always looked up to my grandmother because she raised five children on her own.

cards.definition: To resemble an older family member.
cards.example: I take after my father; we're both quite quiet and patient.

cards.definition: To spend free time somewhere or with someone.
cards.example: On Friday evenings I usually hang out with my flatmates.
cards.note: Perfecto en Speaking Part 1; evítalo en Writing.

cards.definition: To relax.
cards.example: After a long day, I like to chill out by watching a series.

cards.definition: 1) To continue. 2) To happen.
cards.example: I don't know what's going on with the trains this week; they're always late.

cards.definition: To have none left.
cards.example: I ran out of time in the exam and couldn't finish the last question.

cards.definition: 1) To postpone. 2) To discourage.
cards.example: I kept putting off my driving test because I was nervous.

cards.definition: To reduce the amount of something.
cards.example: I'm trying to cut down on sugar and screen time.

cards.definition: To learn informally; to collect someone.
cards.es: aprender sobre la marcha (sin estudiar); recoger
cards.example: I picked up a bit of Italian while I was working in Rome.

cards.definition: To improve a skill you had before.
cards.example: Before the trip I need to brush up on my French.

cards.definition: To investigate or examine.
cards.example: I'm looking into postgraduate courses in Canada at the moment.

cards.definition: To think of an idea or plan.
cards.example: Our team came up with a simple app to help students share notes.
collocations: come up with an idea / solution

cards.definition: To handle or solve.
cards.example: I deal with stress by going for long walks.

cards.definition: To manage successfully in a difficult situation.
cards.example: It was hard to cope with the cold weather during my first winter abroad.

cards.definition: To be easily noticed or better than others.
cards.example: What really stands out about my hometown is its food.

cards.definition: To try to impress others with what you have or can do.
cards.example: Some people use social media just to show off their holidays.

cards.definition: To take care of.
cards.example: My grandparents looked after me while my parents were at work.

cards.definition: To leave / start living in a home.
cards.es: irse a vivir fuera, dejar una casa / instalarse en una casa
cards.example: I moved out of my parents' house when I was 22.

cards.definition: To start a calmer life, often in one place with a family.
cards.example: I'd like to travel for a few years before I settle down.
collocations: settle down and have a family

cards.definition: To refuse an offer; to reduce volume.
cards.example: I turned down a job offer because it meant moving far from my family.

cards.definition: To feel accepted in a group.
cards.example: At first I didn't fit in at my new school, but I soon made friends.

cards.definition: To register for an activity.
cards.example: I've just signed up for an evening pottery class.

cards.definition: To think about the past.
cards.example: When I look back on my school days, I mostly remember the teachers.

cards.definition: To draw attention to a fact.
cards.example: As my teacher once pointed out, mistakes are part of learning.

title: Idioms: natural vs forced
description: 30 expresiones con aviso de cuáles suenan naturales en IELTS Speaking y cuáles suenan memorizadas o trilladas.

cards.definition: It's raining very heavily.
cards.example: Natural alternative: It was pouring down all weekend, so we stayed in.
cards.warning: FORZADA: casi ningún nativo la usa hoy y los examinadores la detectan como memorizada. Di 'it was pouring (down)'.

cards.definition: Very easy.
cards.example: The first part of the course was a piece of cake, but it got harder later.
cards.warning: TRILLADA: correcta pero muy típica de manual; úsala como mucho una vez y nunca para sonar 'avanzado'.

cards.definition: Very rarely.
cards.example: I only eat fast food once in a blue moon.
cards.warning: ARRIESGADA: aceptable, pero muy asociada a listas de 'idioms para IELTS'. 'Hardly ever' o 'very rarely' suenan igual de bien.

cards.definition: Slightly ill.
cards.example: I was feeling a bit under the weather, so I stayed at home.
cards.note: NATURAL: muy usada por nativos para decir que alguien (tú u otra persona) está algo enfermo.

cards.definition: Not something I like.
cards.example: Horror films aren't really my cup of tea; I prefer comedies.
cards.note: NATURAL: suena bien en Part 1 al hablar de gustos.

cards.definition: To start studying hard.
cards.example: With exams in two weeks, I really need to hit the books.

cards.definition: Very busy and active.
cards.es: sin parar, de aquí para allá
cards.example: I'm always on the go during the week, so I value quiet weekends.

cards.definition: Over a long period of time; eventually.
cards.example: Learning to cook saves you a lot of money in the long run.
cards.note: NATURAL y útil también en Writing y Part 3.

cards.definition: To sound familiar.
cards.example: The name rings a bell, but I can't remember where I heard it.

cards.term: cost an arm and a leg
cards.definition: To be very expensive.
cards.es: costar un ojo de la cara
cards.example: Renting a flat in the city centre costs an arm and a leg.
cards.note: NATURAL, aunque muy conocida: no la repitas.

cards.term: on the tip of my tongue
cards.definition: Almost remembered.
cards.es: en la punta de la lengua
cards.example: The word is on the tip of my tongue... ah yes, 'nostalgic'.
cards.note: NATURAL y además te salva cuando no recuerdas una palabra en el examen.

cards.definition: To widen your experience and knowledge.
cards.example: Studying abroad really broadened my horizons.

cards.definition: The advantages of two different things.
cards.es: lo mejor de los dos mundos
cards.example: Living in a small town near a big city gives you the best of both worlds.

cards.definition: To feel both positive and negative.
cards.example: I have mixed feelings about social media: it's useful but addictive.
cards.note: NATURAL; excelente para matizar opiniones en Part 3.

cards.definition: To not appreciate something because it's always there.
cards.example: We often take clean water for granted.

cards.definition: To stay in contact.
cards.example: I keep in touch with my school friends through a group chat.

cards.definition: To have just enough money to live.
cards.example: Many students work part-time just to make ends meet.
cards.note: NATURAL; útil en temas de trabajo y economía.

cards.definition: Something you do automatically.
cards.example: After a few months, cycling in traffic became second nature.

cards.definition: To learn how to do a job.
cards.example: My first week at the café was spent learning the ropes.

cards.definition: Unexpectedly.
cards.example: An old friend called me out of the blue last month.

cards.definition: Extremely happy.
cards.example: I was over the moon when I got my university place.
cards.note: NATURAL, sobre todo en inglés británico; no la uses para cosas pequeñas.

cards.definition: To make people feel relaxed when they first meet.
cards.example: Our teacher used a quick game to break the ice on the first day.
cards.note: NATURAL (y funciona igual que en español).

cards.term: hit the nail on the head
cards.definition: To describe something exactly right.
cards.example: I think the article hit the nail on the head about why young people can't buy houses.

cards.term: every cloud has a silver lining
cards.definition: Every bad situation has some good aspect.
cards.es: no hay mal que por bien no venga
cards.example: I missed my flight, but there was a silver lining: I met my best friend at the airport.
cards.warning: FORZADA: los refranes completos suenan a recitado. Mejor: 'there was a silver lining, though'.

cards.term: the early bird catches the worm
cards.definition: People who start early succeed.
cards.es: a quien madruga, Dios le ayuda
cards.example: I'm an early bird; I do my best work before 9am.
cards.warning: FORZADA como refrán completo. 'I'm an early bird / a morning person' sí es natural.

cards.definition: What you do matters more than what you say.
cards.es: obras son amores y no buenas razones
cards.example: Politicians promise a lot, but actions speak louder than words, so I judge them by what they do.
cards.warning: TRILLADA: correcta pero suena a frase hecha memorizada si la metes sin motivo.

cards.term: an apple a day keeps the doctor away
cards.definition: Healthy eating prevents illness.
cards.example: Natural alternative: I try to eat fruit every day because it helps me stay healthy.
cards.warning: FORZADA: muy infantil para el examen. Penaliza más que suma.

cards.term: kill two birds with one stone
cards.definition: To achieve two things with one action.
cards.es: matar dos pájaros de un tiro
cards.example: Cycling to work kills two birds with one stone: I save money and get fit.
cards.warning: ARRIESGADA: natural, pero de las más sobreutilizadas por candidatos. Úsala sólo si encaja de verdad.

cards.definition: Something bad that turns out to be good.
cards.es: no hay mal que por bien no venga; algo malo que resultó ser bueno
cards.example: Failing my first driving test was a blessing in disguise; I became a much safer driver.
cards.note: NATURAL si cuentas una historia real (útil en Part 2).

cards.definition: To have very little time.
cards.example: I'm usually pressed for time in the mornings, so I skip breakfast.
